neighbours.label: free-choice 'any' (any kind, any setting, on any terms): 'any' meaning 'whichever you pick' in an affirmative claim, not polarity 'any' in questions or negations
fire: Such courage would be remarkable in any era, let alone during a famine.
The coat is warm enough for weather of any sort in the mountains.
She would have stood out in any classroom she walked into.
The rule applies to drivers of any age who hold a licence.
This is a dangerous plan by any measure, and the board knows it.
Good bread is welcome at a table in any country of the world.
He was willing to accept peace on any conditions the king set.
A single spark in any corner of the barn could start a fire.
quiet: Did they find any survivors after the famine in the north?
The coat is not warm enough for any weather in the mountains.
She has hardly any friends in the classroom yet.
Are there any drivers here who hold a licence?
The board has not seen any figures for this dangerous plan.
We could not find any bread on the table this morning.
He did not accept the conditions the king set for peace.
A single spark in the corner of the barn started a fire.
